findings.evidence: `roadmap/TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves/Suggested.lean:668` specifies `def IsSemistable (W : WeierstrassCurve K) [W.IsElliptic]`; `Mathlib/.../Reduction.lean:347` and `:354` define `HasMultiplicativeReduction` and `HasAdditiveReduction` without an `IsElliptic` premise.
findings.fix: Add `[W.IsElliptic]` to `IsSemistable` as specified by the roadmap and propagate the instance through every theorem using it (and the local criterion if it is presented as an elliptic reduction theorem).
findings.issue: `IsSemistable` and its API at lines 118–175 omit `[W.IsElliptic]`; Mathlib's reduction predicates themselves impose no ellipticity, so this genuinely admits singular equations and makes “good or multiplicative reduction” an invalid elliptic-curve classification.

summary: `IsSemistable` is defined for arbitrary Weierstrass equations, so singular equations can be classified as semistable despite the intended elliptic-curve scope.
